data.name: Enceladus
data.detailed_description:
"Far down the road in Human history, an abnormality in space-time suddently appeared on one of Saturn's moon : Encelade.

Spaceships of an unknown origin take the human fleet by surprise. A real genocide.

Earth also seems to be overwhelmed by the assault and only a small group, scouting near Encelade manageto avoid the attack. By approching the icy surface of the moon there is still one last hope of a counter attack againt the ennemy from another world."


Enceladus is a shoot'em up inspired by the Playstation & Saturn era infused with mecanical gameplay and modern artistic style.

Easy to handle, skill will be needed in order to beat the 7 levels available.

The player takes control of « Frost », a spaceship capable of firing energy blast or to channel a very powerful laser. He also has the ability to trigger a powerful explosion, ideal to get yourself out of trouble.

The number one asset of « Frost » is his ability to teleport. By a simple push of a button, it is possible to create a ghost of Frost while still defending yourself. By letting go of that same button « Frost » teleports to the ghost's location.

That technology allows you to move faster, to dodge overwhelming shots but also to gain acces to unaccessable zones.

Teleportation needs practice, but once mastered « Frost » becomes so much harder to destroy.

reviews.review:
Enceladus is a retro-inspired side-scrolling shoot’em-up that embraces the spirit of arcade classics while introducing enough original ideas to stand apart from the crowd. Developed by Storybird and Julien Rocca and published by Look At My Game and Plug In Digital, the game presents a science-fiction conflict set around Saturn’s icy moon, where humanity faces annihilation at the hands of an enigmatic alien force. Although the story serves mainly as a backdrop for the action, it establishes a fitting sense of urgency and gives players a reason to push deeper into the hostile reaches of space.

What immediately separates Enceladus from many traditional shooters is its innovative teleportation mechanic. Rather than relying solely on precise movement and memorization, players command the spacecraft Frost, which can leave behind a temporary marker and instantly warp back to that position. This ability adds an entirely new strategic layer to the experience. Dodging enemy fire becomes less about reacting at the last second and more about planning ahead. Skilled players can use teleportation to bypass dangerous situations, avoid dense bullet formations, and discover alternate routes hidden throughout the levels. It is a simple concept on paper, but it fundamentally changes how encounters are approached and gives the game its unique identity.

The combat system supports this mechanic with a satisfying arsenal of offensive options. Standard weapons provide consistent damage output, while a powerful laser attack allows players to focus on stronger enemies and bosses. In addition, a screen-clearing special attack offers a valuable escape tool during overwhelming moments. These abilities create a rewarding balance between offense and defense, encouraging players to carefully manage resources while maintaining an aggressive playstyle. The result is gameplay that remains engaging throughout the campaign rather than becoming repetitive or overly dependent on memorization.

Level design is another area where Enceladus performs well. Across its seven stages, the game gradually introduces new enemy formations, environmental hazards, and increasingly challenging encounters. Each stage feels designed around the core mechanics rather than simply serving as a backdrop for waves of enemies. The hidden areas accessible through clever use of teleportation provide an extra incentive to replay levels, adding a sense of discovery that is often absent from more straightforward shooters. This design philosophy rewards experimentation and encourages players to refine their strategies with every run.

Visually, the game successfully channels the aesthetics of late-1990s arcade and console shooters. Detailed pixel art, vibrant visual effects, and varied science-fiction environments create a nostalgic atmosphere without feeling outdated. The frozen landscapes associated with Enceladus and the futuristic spacecraft designs help establish a distinctive setting, while explosions and enemy animations provide enough visual excitement to keep the action lively. Although the production values are modest compared to larger modern releases, the presentation demonstrates a clear passion for the genre and remains consistently appealing throughout the adventure.

The audio design complements the visuals effectively. The soundtrack enhances the futuristic atmosphere and maintains the energy required for an action-focused experience. Sound effects are crisp and impactful, giving weight to weapon fire, explosions, and special abilities. Together, the audio and visual elements help create a cohesive arcade experience that feels authentic to its inspirations while retaining its own character.

Despite its strengths, Enceladus is not entirely free of shortcomings. Some players may find the overall campaign relatively short, especially compared to modern games that emphasize extensive content. The title is clearly built around replayability, mastery, and score chasing rather than a lengthy narrative-driven journey. Technical and customization limitations may also frustrate some users, particularly those who prefer extensive controller support and graphical options. These issues do not undermine the core gameplay, but they can affect the overall experience for certain players.

Ultimately, Enceladus succeeds because it understands what makes classic shoot’em-ups enjoyable while introducing a genuinely creative mechanic that alters the traditional formula. The teleportation system adds meaningful depth, the combat remains satisfying, and the level design consistently encourages experimentation and mastery. While its limited scope and technical shortcomings prevent it from becoming a genre-defining masterpiece, it remains an entertaining and inventive shooter that offers something different from many of its contemporaries. Fans of classic arcade action and players seeking a fresh twist on established shoot’em-up mechanics will find plenty to appreciate in this overlooked space adventure.

Rating: 6/10
